stories.headline: Iran's Guards declare Hormuz 'closed' after reported tanker mine strikes
stories.blurb: On Saturday Iran's IRGC said two supertankers carrying about 2 million barrels each hit mines on an 'unauthorized' route; one caught fire. There is no independent confirmation, and the US says commercial shipping continues. UK maritime monitors logged a record weekly count of ship attacks near the strait. — Oil rose about 10% WoW into Friday; a fresh leg up on Monday would add to inflation and hike worries and test BTC's $80k floor alongside stocks.

stories.headline: BTC holds ~$81k through a quiet weekend; month's gain fades to flat
stories.blurb: Bitcoin traded in a narrow band around $81.4k on Saturday and Sunday, above Thursday's ~$79.8k low. It is down about 2.6% WoW, and barely up MoM (under 1%) now that mid-September's lows have dropped out of the comparison. — Calm weekend trade plus rising leverage means the next move could be sharp; $80k below and ~$84k above are the levels to watch.

stories.headline: Full-week ETF tally: outflows about a third of the prior week's
stories.blurb: With Friday's IBIT print in, US spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $228M over Oct 12–16 versus about $679M the week before; ether ETFs also lost less. CoinShares counted $434M of outflows across global crypto funds. No sessions over the weekend. — Demand is still not buying the dip, but selling pressure has eased — the floor looks less fragile than a week ago.

stories.headline: MSCI adopts screens that could drop crypto-treasury companies
stories.blurb: MSCI's new eligibility rules for companies without substantial operating assets take effect at the Nov 30 close, with a final list due Nov 11. Strategy and Metaplanet were among potential deletions in an earlier simulation; their status is unresolved. — Index removal could force passive selling of treasury-company shares — a slow-burn sentiment risk for BTC into November.

With mid-September's lows rolling out of the comparison, the month is now roughly flat. BTC still fell less than the Nasdaq and kept $80k. The full week's ETF tally came in at about a third of the prior week's outflows: still selling, but less. Over the weekend Iran's Guards called Hormuz closed after reported tanker mine strikes, which puts oil and stocks at risk on Monday. Futures leverage is still building into weakness. ~$80k below and ~$84k above frame the week.
